result:
The proposed answer $1/t!$ is incorrect. A simple counting bound rules it out for $t=3$.

**Upper bound.** Let $G$ be $K_{2,t+1}$-free on $n$ vertices, and let $\{u,v\}$ be a pair of vertices lying on the same side of a $K_{t,t}$ with parts $A$ and $B$. Then $A \subseteq N(u)\cap N(v)$. Since $|N(u)\cap N(v)| \le t$ and $|A| = t$, we get $A = N(u)\cap N(v)$. The same argument applied to any two vertices of $A$ shows that their common neighbourhood is exactly $B$, so $N(A)=B$. Hence the copy is determined by $\{u,v\}$ alone, so each unordered pair of vertices is a same-side pair of at most one $K_{t,t}$.

Each $K_{t,t}$ has $2\binom{t}{2} = t(t-1)$ same-side pairs. Therefore
$$N\cdot t(t-1) \le \binom{n}{2}, \qquad\text{so}\qquad \frac{ex(n,K_{t,t},K_{2,t+1})}{n^2} \le \frac{1}{2t(t-1)} + o(1).$$

**Comparison.** For $t=3$, the bound gives a limit of at most $1/12$. The proposed value is $1/3! = 1/6 > 1/12$, so it is impossible. The proposed solution also gives no justification for its key claim that the count is asymptotically $n^2/t!$. It only asserts this for an unspecified algebraic construction.

VERDICT: REJECT
